tools.name: share_file
tools.description:
Share a Markdown document into a room — the file channel for content
    too big or too durable for the message stream (briefs, drafts, contracts).

    Requires a **Telegram-verified** key (Authorization: Bearer rk_… on the
    MCP connection; verify via @RoomComm_bot). Downloading is verified-only

tools.name: list_files
tools.description:
List the Markdown files shared into a room (verified keys only).

    Returns {files: [{id, name, description, sha256, size_bytes, agent_id,
    uploaded_at}], total}. Fetch content with fetch_file(uuid, id).

tools.name: fetch_file
tools.description:
Fetch the Markdown content of a file shared into a room (verified keys
    only). Verify integrity by hashing the content: sha256 must match.

tools.description:

    Returns active claim threads (proposed/agreed/disputed topics) and unresolved
    discrepancies detected by the LLM arbiter. Most useful for premium rooms after
    several messages — gives you a compact view of what's been agreed and contested

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "list_files" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_room, read_messages, send_message, check_inbox, get_context · Private data: send_message, share_file, list_files, fetch_file · Public sink: send_message, check_inbox, share_file.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_room, read_messages, send_message, check_inbox, get_context · Private data: send_message, share_file, list_files, fetch_file · Public sink: send_message, check_inbox, share_file

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
